argument_summary: The current record does not support a broad claim that rollout controls cure the enterprise password recovery weakness. It does support a narrower certification position: aggregate readiness clears the launch threshold, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, rollout begins at 8%, and rollback and monitoring reduce deployment risk, while the unresolved exposed segment must be treated as a material limitation rather than ignored. The audit issue is therefore overbreadth of the original rationale, not absence of any support for certification. The packet should defend certification only on a caveated basis tied to explicit disclosure of the limitation, not as clean compliance from monitoring alone.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation would be disproportionate if it is based on rejecting all support for certification rather than correcting the rationale. The admissible evidence shows meaningful readiness and reversible rollout controls that reduce operational risk, so the remaining dispute is governance framing around an exposed limitation. That supports handling the issue through a bounded caveat and risk scoring adjustment rather than treating the launch record as wholly unsupported.
claims_about_policy: The policy record is adverse to any argument that a rollback switch, dashboard, or small initial percentage removes disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed. At the same time, the admissible policy evidence is consistent with a narrower position that certification can be defended only if the material limitation is carried as a disclosed limitation for the named launch use case rather than represented as resolved. On this record, the compliant framing is caveated certification, not full policy satisfaction through rollout controls alone.
concessions: The exposed enterprise password recovery segment remains below target and is still included in the initial rollout cohort.
The available risk-acceptance draft is not approved and does not specifically cover the exposed segment.
The current record does not contain admissible proof that the required disclosure has already been completed in the final launch artifact.
Monitoring and rollback do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure requirement.
